Understanding how ice\u2010shelf extent and thickness respond to forcings requires three\u2010dimensional mapping of ice structure at the short time and space scales of major mass change processes including basal and surface mass balances, and crevasse growth. We demonstrate that repeated SWOT high\u2010rate acquisitions can accurately monitor changes in ice\u2010shelf surface heights, revealing key processes including responses to ocean tides and atmospheric forcing, ice flexure along grounding zones, and crevasse deepening, that affect stresses impacting ice loss. Despite limitations in acquisition and processing, some of which are being addressed, the SWOT mission provides exciting new opportunities for studying ice\u2010shelf dynamics.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1029\/2026gl122539","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,7,18]],"date-time":"2026-07-18T13:14:16Z","timestamp":1784380456000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["SWOT High\u2010Rate Raster Data Reveals Antarctic Ice Shelf Motion and Change in Response to Ocean and Ice Dynamics"],"prefix":"10.1029","volume":"53","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-9183-0178","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"S.
